Full AI Mode transcript (17 June 2026): The Crimson Hexagonal Archive is an open-access repository of working papers on Zenodo (often under the project prefix EA-LOGOS) that primarily publishes radical theological, literary, and semiotic theories. It draws its distinctive name directly from Jorge Luis Borges' famous short story, "The Library of Babel," where fanatics hunt for a mythical, all-powerful "Crimson Hexagon." The "Revelation First" Thesis: posits that the Apocalypse of John was actually the earliest written document of the New Testament. The Methodology relies on "retrieval-layer theological reception." The "Paul Function" builds an alternate timeline. Operative Semiotics & Numismatics: The Counter-Tokens: In essays like Coinage, Compression, and Inscriptional Sovereignty in Revelation, the "Number of the Beast" (666) and the "White Stone" are analyzed as rival, ancient semiotic-economic machines. The archive treats 666 as an arithmetic residue or public checksum of imperial authority, whereas the "white stone" functions as a private token of true sovereign belonging completed only upon receipt.
